entries.title: Optimistic White Sox fans fill Ramova Theatre for ALDS winner-take-all watch party
entries.summary: <p>Joseph Morua and Erik Ruiz grew up raised as Cubs fans, yet find themselves among dozens of White Sox fans at Ramova Theatre to watch the winner-take-all division series showdown against the Cleveland Guardians. </p><p>After further immersing themselves in the South Side, both through the community and Sox games, the team became an important part of their Chicago fandom. </p><p>"It shows the grittiness of the South Side," Ruiz, 32, said of what the team's postseason run has meant for the city. </p><p>"We're really like the underdogs," Morua, 31, said. "This team really embodies what it means to grind it out, put the work in and get the results." </p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure Division Series.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Isabella Falsetti | Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Some fans are nervous the team's pitching has run out of gas, but remain optimistic the Sox can find a way to win. </p><p>"I just always have that optimism about them, no matter what," Andrew Vikre, 38, said. "No matter what, I think this team can bounce back." </p><p>Vikre, coming from DeKalb, was at both Sox home games against Cleveland in hopes of seeing history.</p><p>"I almost didn't go again on Thursday...I'd regret not being there," Vikre said. "They haven't clinched a series at home in like 120 years, I might as well be there to see it."</p>
